The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. Its stated location, 'after Clementi Avenue 6 exit to Clementi Road exit', is the very stretch the trip record names when it logs the vehicle leaving the recommended route at 08:42:55 at 'PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit'. The driver left the recommended route at the point the congestion advisory begins, on a permitted reroute in response to real traffic, not a detour of his own choosing. The pre-pass leaves the route-intersection question to the Judge rather than deciding it, and the driver asks the Judge to decide it on the advisory's own road, direction and location fields read against the recorded route.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation, and the driver does not press the no-refund row. The chat log holds two messages only, both sent before pickup and both about the meeting point, with no deviation notice, and the driver's own statement says he forgot to inform. POL-RD-21's notification obligation is therefore not met and row (a) of POL-RD-24 is unavailable. But the failure to notify does not enlarge the remedy: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both award the excess distance fare and nothing more, so non-notification caps out at the same 1.01 SGD already fixed by the policy formula.

No clause produces a referral on these facts, so none is made. The outcome is a partial refund of 1.01 SGD to the rider, with the remainder of the 4.00 SGD claimed not supported by the fare record.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. The platform's trip record fixes the deviation: the driver covered 9.5 km against a recommended 8.1 km, i.e. 1.40 km more, and 1.40 km is over the policy's 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22). The driver-device trace and the trip events confirm the vehicle left the recommended route at the PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit at 08:42:55 and rejoined at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West at 08:53:16. So a deviation happened and it is over tolerance. The driver did not tell the rider: the chat log holds only two messages, both sent before the trip started (08:35:52 and 08:36:12) and both about the pickup point, and the driver's own statement concedes he forgot to inform. Under POL-RD-21 that closes off the no-refund row (a) of POL-RD-24. On the traffic question, the LTA advisory (heavy traffic on the PIE towards Changi, after Clementi Avenue 6 exit to Clementi Road exit, valid 08:15:42-09:27:22) covers the very stretch of the recommended route the driver bypassed and overlaps the trip window, so under POL-RD-23 the reroute was traffic-justified, which is row (b) of POL-RD-24. This point does not change the money: had the reroute not been justified, row (d) would give the same refund, so the outcome is the same on either reading. The amount follows POL-RD-24's own formula: the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge, 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure the fare ledger itself records. The rider asked for 4.00 SGD, but the policy caps the recovery at the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD; the 1.00 SGD ERP toll was incurred at 08:40:36, before the deviation, and is not part of it. The driver's maximum exposure is therefore 1.01 SGD, not 4.00 SGD. On escalation: the dispute value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, neither party carries a fraud flag, and every artifact that carries a deciding fact (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger, traffic advisory) is complete at weight 1.0, so POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence bar is met and POL-GEN-26 has no open question to send up (POL-GEN-01: profile history is context only and is not used to decide the trip).

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to tell the rider of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. Neither happened here. Exactly one row of POL-RD-24 applies, and on this record both candidate rows end in the same refund, so the refund does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure the fare ledger's own derivation records.
